speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You present with double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; to begin my assessment, have you noticed if your double vision worsens when you look up or down, and does your difficulty climbing stairs improve with rest?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.

The pattern of double vision worsening with upward/downward gaze and fluctuating weakness that improves with rest is classic for Myasthenia Gravis. To confirm this diagnosis, I am requesting your antibody test results and a Chest_X-Ray to check for thymoma.
